sbh2.3:1.4: having established the benefit-aspiration, [it is] the resolve to bring mild, middling, or strong happiness —
sbh2.3:1.5: a resolve grounded in the concentrated plane.
sbh2.3:1.9: The benefit-aspiration and the resolve to bring happiness, grounded in the concentrated plane — this is the operator.
sbh2.3:1.11: and the operator, combined into one — this is called lovingkindness.
sbh2.3:2.1: When [the canonical formula] says 'with mind imbued with lovingkindness,' by this the benefit-aspiration is named, [extending] through the three sides — friend, enemy, neutral.
sbh2.3:2.3: 'without enmity, without opposition, without harming' — by this, the threefold characteristic of that benefit-aspiration is named.
sbh2.3:2.4: Of these: by non-enmity, the benefit-aspiration [is characterized]. This non-enmity is named by two further terms:
sbh2.3:2.6: Non-opposition is so named because it has the sense of being-without-an-opposing-stance.
sbh2.3:2.7: Non-harming is so named because it has the sense of being-without-malice-and-injury.
sbh2.3:3.2: 'vast, exalted, immeasurable' — by this, the bringing of mild, middling, or strong happiness is named:
sbh2.3:3.3: happiness of the desire-realm, or of the first-and-second-absorption planes, or of the third-absorption plane.
sbh2.3:3.5: [Damaged/Conjectural]: 'having attained, he abides resolved upon' — by this, the resolve to bring happiness, grounded in the concentrated plane, is named.
sbh2.3:4.1: This bringing of happiness, encompassed by the benefit-aspiration,
sbh2.3:4.4: should be understood as directed toward those who are neither-suffering-nor-happy, desiring happiness, on the friend-side, enemy-side, or neutral-side.
sbh2.3:4.5: Whereas for the one who is suffering, or the non-suffering [that is, happy] one, on the friend-side,
sbh2.3:4.7: the suffering one is the object of compassion;
sbh2.3:4.8: the happy one is the object of sympathetic joy. This is called lovingkindness.
sbh2.3:5.1: The ill-will-conduct person, cultivating lovingkindness, attenuates the ill-will toward beings.
sbh2.3:5.2: He purifies the mind from ill-will.
